key_insight: DocTalk’s chart-grounded instruction tuning improved medical question-answering performance across six open-source language models.
clinical_relevance: The system could help clinicians retrieve information from discharge summaries, but improved benchmark performance does not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Generated 500 QA pairs from de-identified discharge summaries using sentence decomposition, chain-of-thought-guided question formulation, and expert review.
Evaluated three general-purpose and three biomedical models before and after LoRA instruction tuning.
Tested the two top-performing models on PubMedQA to assess external generalization.
evidence_signal: Tuned Llama-3-Med42-8B achieved ROUGE-L 0.40, BERTScore-F1 0.76, and UMLS-F1 0.49; PubMedQA accuracy rose from 93.1% to 97.7% for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and from 93.5% to 94.3% for Med42.
watch_item: The abstract reports a small, 500-pair dataset and benchmark evaluations, not prospective evidence of safe use in clinical workflows.
paper_title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support
